Structure-adaptive spatial FDR (SABHA)

Source: R/posthoc-fdr-sabha.R
spatial_fdr_sabha.Rd

Voxel-level spatially aware FDR control by a structure-adaptive weighted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Each feature belongs to a spatial group (parcel, block, cluster); the proportion of nulls \(\pi_0\) is estimated per group (Storey), optionally smoothed over neighbouring groups, and the weighted BH procedure of Genovese, Roeder & Wasserman (2006) is applied with weights \(1/\pi_0\) normalised to sum to the number of finite p-values: reject \(p_i \le w_i \alpha k / n\). Unlike posthoc() method "fdr:spatial" (Simes aggregation, one q-value per parcel), every feature keeps its own q-value. Results are identical to fmrireg::spatial_fdr().

Usage

spatial_fdr_sabha(
  z = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  group,
  alpha = 0.05,
  tau = 0.5,
  lambda = 1,
  neighbors = NULL,
  min_pi0 = 0.05,
  empirical_null = TRUE
)

Arguments

z

Numeric vector (or features x maps matrix) of z-values. Supply either z or p.

p

Numeric vector (or matrix) of two-sided p-values.

group

Integer, character or factor vector of group ids, one per feature (row).

alpha

FDR level in (0, 1); sets reject, threshold and k (q-values do not depend on it).

tau

Storey threshold in (0, 1) for \(\pi_0\) estimation.

lambda

Non-negative smoothing strength of \(\pi_0\) across neighbours (one step of \((\pi_g + \lambda \bar\pi_{N(g)})/(1+\lambda)\)).

neighbors

Optional list of length G; element g holds the 1-based ids (in the numbering above) of the neighbours of group g.

min_pi0

Lower bound in [0, 1] for the smoothed \(\pi_0\).

empirical_null

Logical; estimate \(\mu_0, \sigma_0\) from z.

Value

For vector input, a list with reject, q, p (the p-values tested), weights (normalised), pi0_raw, pi0_smooth, threshold, k, mu0, sigma0, groups (1..G ids), G, m_g (features per group), alpha, tau, lambda. For matrix input every column is processed independently: reject, q, p, weights are matrices, pi0_raw/pi0_smooth are G x columns, and threshold, k, mu0, sigma0 are per-column vectors.

Details

Group numbering. Groups are numbered 1..G by sorted unique value, or by factor level (unused levels included) when group is a factor. This numbering indexes neighbors, pi0_raw, pi0_smooth and m_g. Features with NA group are excluded from \(\pi_0\) estimation and receive weight 1 before normalisation.

Empirical null. When z is supplied with empirical_null = TRUE, \(\mu_0\) and \(\sigma_0\) are estimated by Efron's (2004) central matching: a quadratic is fitted by Poisson regression to the log histogram counts of z within \(\pm 1.5\) robust SDs of the median. With fewer than 500 finite z-values (or if the fit fails) the median and normal-consistent MAD of all finite z-values are used instead; with fewer than 10 the theoretical null is used. p-values are then two-sided normal p-values of \((z - \mu_0)/\sigma_0\).

References

Benjamini & Hochberg (1995); Storey (2002); Genovese, Roeder & Wasserman (2006) False discovery control with p-value weighting; Efron (2004) Large-scale simultaneous hypothesis testing: the choice of a null hypothesis.

See also

posthoc-methods ("fdr:sabha"), posthoc()

Examples

set.seed(1)
grp <- rep(1:10, each = 100)
z <- rnorm(1000)
z[grp <= 2] <- z[grp <= 2] + 3
res <- spatial_fdr_sabha(z = z, group = grp, alpha = 0.05)
sum(res$reject)
#> [1] 86
res$pi0_smooth
#>  [1] 0.05 0.05 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 0.90 1.00 1.00
